question: Ines had 182 photographs in her shoebox before the exhibition. She had 45 more prints made and dropped them into the same box. She gave 141 of the photographs to the families who appear in them, and 8 more were spoiled when a window was left open in the rain. She spread what remained equally across 6 display boards, then hung only one of those boards in the hall and stored the rest. A dozen visitors came to the opening. Every photograph on the hall board was held up with 8 brass tacks. How many tacks were used on the hall board?

Aiko opened the plant in the morning with 164 sealed cases in the loading bay, and every case contained 9 component trays. Each of those trays was packed with 7 memory chips. Her colleague Bram arrived before lunch with 26 loose chips from the test bench, and they were counted in with the others. During the afternoon the buyer valued every chip at 5 credits. In the evening the accounts office converted each credit into 8 supplier points. The points were then split equally among the 5 production teams. How many points went to the team Aiko leads?

The Carfax Museum counted 130 visitors through its doors before ten o'clock. Another 59 came in during the late morning. The lunchtime hour brought a further 79 people, and 33 more arrived in the middle of the afternoon. The museum has 12 galleries spread over two wings. In the evening, during the late opening, 62 visitors came through. How many visitors did the museum have that day?

A small plant shop had 38 potted cacti on its stands at the start of the fair, and it opens 5 days a week. During the fair 36 of the cacti were sold to visitors. On the Monday afterwards a grower delivered 28 new cacti to the shop. The owner divided all the cacti equally across 3 shelves, kept the window shelf in the shop and sent the other shelves to a sister branch. That spring every cactus on the window shelf opened 6 flowers. How many flowers opened on the window shelf?

The school canteen had 198 bread rolls in its warm cabinet at the start of the day, and the kitchen weighs its flour in grams rather than in kilograms. Breakfast service took 84 rolls out of the cabinet. A delivery van brought 10 rolls mid-morning, and the baker pulled 66 more out of the oven before noon. Every roll was then sliced into 3 pieces for the sandwich bar, tripling the count on the counter. Lunch service used 468 of those pieces, and 45 untouched pieces came back from the staff room afterwards. The canteen seats 240 pupils. How many pieces were left at the end of the day?

The Larkhill apiary kept 169 hives on the hillside last spring, and the farm around it covers 40 hectares. A pollination contract moved 151 of those hives to an orchard fifty miles away for the whole season. Every hive that stayed on the hillside holds 7 wooden frames. Each frame carries 9 separate combs of honey. When the combs were spun, each one filled 9 jars. The store room already held 9 jars from the previous autumn, and they were counted with the new ones. How many jars were in the store room?

Yuki folded 58 paper cranes during the first week of the memorial project. She sent 30 of them to the children's hospital straight away. Her whole class then joined in, and the number of cranes she held tripled, becoming 3 times what she had. A friend from another school posted her 61 more cranes. When the display went up, volunteers folded a matching crane for every one Yuki had, so the display held twice as many. Each crane on the display was hung on a thread with 4 glass beads. How many beads were used on the display?

Ana picked 14 tomatoes from her allotment on Saturday morning and 4 more from the same plants that afternoon. Her neighbour Piet, whose greenhouse had done far better than her plot, handed her 31 of his tomatoes over the fence. Ana cooked 39 of the tomatoes into sauce for the freezer. From each tomato that was left she saved 7 seeds for the next season. When she tested the saved seeds, 56 of them were hollow and she threw those away. How many seeds did Ana keep?

A theatre printed 221 programmes for each of the 2 opening nights, so the print run was double the single-night figure. Ushers handed out 313 programmes over those two nights. A stagehand then found 50 unopened programmes in a props box and added them to the pile. The theatre has 18 rows in the stalls, and the box office records running times in minutes rather than in hours. For the tour the printer produced triple the surviving pile, making 3 copies of every programme. Later 235 of those copies were sent for recycling. How many programmes remained?

Sofia had 68 sticker sheets, and every sheet carried 6 stickers. She and her cousin Luis shared all the stickers equally between 4 boxes, and Sofia took just one box home while the other boxes stayed at his house. The arcade in town is open 11 hours a day. There, each sticker in her box was exchanged for 9 game tokens. A weekend promotion then tripled her tokens, giving her 3 times as many. She spent 92 tokens on the racing machine, and every token she had left was later converted into 9 loyalty points. How many loyalty points did Sofia end up with?

A county archive stores its atlases on 85 long shelves, with 9 atlases standing on each shelf. Half of those shelves are down in the basement, and the archive records the age of a document in months rather than in years. Every atlas in the building contains 4 fold-out maps. A survey found that 706 of the maps were too badly foxed to keep, and they were withdrawn. A partner archive in the next county then borrowed 428 of the remaining maps for an exhibition. How many maps were still held in the county archive?

Priyanka set out 123 paper cups at the halfway water station of a road race. Her fellow volunteer Noor brought 20 more cups from the gazebo, and the supply van dropped off 61 additional cups. The race itself is 42 kilometres long. A gust of wind blew 19 cups off the table and they had to be binned. Every cup on the table was used twice during the race, so 2 servings were poured from each one. Each serving was given 5 ice cubes, and the cooler still held 47 spare cubes that were counted in as well. How many ice cubes were counted at the station?

Jonah had 94 coins saved in a jar on his windowsill. His grandmother gave him 42 coins for his birthday, and he earned 26 more coins doing jobs around the house. Half of his friends keep savings jars too. He then spent 152 coins on a second-hand board game at the market. Clearing out the sofa the next weekend, he found 6 coins and dropped them into the jar. How many coins were in Jonah's jar afterwards?

The community orchard began the season with 28 apple trees along its west path. The volunteers planted 59 new trees in the spring and another 16 in early summer. Later that year disease forced them to take out 54 trees, which were burned at the edge of the field. Every tree still standing gave 4 crates of apples at harvest. A neighbouring smallholder donated 4 crates of his own to the orchard shop, and the committee bought 78 crates from a farm in the next valley to meet its orders. How many crates did the orchard shop have?

Sam kept 130 comic books in a crate under his bed, far more than his cousin Ines, who had only a thin pile of her own. He sold 34 of his comics to Ines when she started collecting seriously. Damp in the cellar ruined 3 more of his comics and he threw them out. At a convention Sam made a swap so good that his collection tripled, ending at 3 times what he had carried in. He then donated 193 comics to the hospital reading room. How many comics did Sam have left?

A stone quarry loaded 77 pallets one week, and each pallet carried 8 rough slabs. Half of the quarry's output is sold outside the country. Every slab was later cut into 6 floor tiles at the finishing shed. Inspection found 431 tiles cracked and they were sent back to be crushed. A builders merchant bought 1218 of the tiles, and the council took 857 more for the new town square. How many tiles were still in the finishing shed?

The mountain hostel counted 132 blankets in its store cupboard at the end of the season. The warden sent 29 of them down to the valley laundry and they did not come back in time. A supplier delivered 61 new blankets the following week. Another 2 blankets were torn beyond repair when a shelf collapsed. A dozen walkers checked in that evening. The warden then gave 147 blankets to a shelter in the town below. How many blankets were left in the store cupboard?

The campaign team loaded 7 vans on the first morning, and each van carried 210 leaflets. A dozen volunteers met them at the town hall. Before noon 174 leaflets were handed out at the market. The printer then ran off 66 extra leaflets and these were added to the vans. Rain soaked 20 leaflets while a door was open, and they were binned. Through the afternoon and early evening 1130 leaflets were posted through letterboxes, and the team notes its walking distances in metres rather than in kilometres. How many leaflets were still in the vans at nightfall?

A printing studio pulled 202 proof sheets from its old press. It found 24 of them badly misregistered and destroyed them. Each remaining sheet was then stamped 6 separate times to make a set of impressions. The impressions were filed equally into 6 identical folders, and the studio kept one folder for the archive while selling the rest. Every impression in the archive folder was rated at 5 collector points. Judges deducted 7 points for smudging, and the studio later traded 115 points to another archive. How many collector points did the studio hold at the end?

A haberdashery keeps 123 spools of ribbon in its back room, and it records thread length in centimetres rather than in metres. Over the winter 49 spools were used up on wedding orders. The owner then gave 34 spools to the local drama club for costumes. Every spool still in the back room was wound out onto 9 display cards. Each display card was finished with 4 matching buttons pinned along its edge. How many buttons were pinned in total?

Hana came home from the market with 51 boiled sweets, and the stall sells them by the gram rather than by the kilogram. On the way home 3 of the sweets fell into a puddle and had to be thrown away. She shared what was left equally with her brother Ravi, so the pile split into 2 equal halves and she kept hers. Over the next week Hana ate 14 of her own sweets. She then divided her remaining sweets equally between 2 small tins and posted one tin to her grandmother. How many sweets were in the tin she posted?

A school district ordered 239 packs of pencils for each of its 7 year groups. The stockroom manager, Mr Dane, found 49 forgotten packs on a high shelf and 18 packs in the art cupboard. His colleague Mrs Oyelaran, whose own store proved richer than his, contributed 59 packs from the science block and 54 packs from the library. Every pack in the district holds 7 pencils, and the stock list is kept in single pencils rather than in boxes. How many pencils does the district have?

A potter finished 53 bowls for the craft fair, and her kiln reaches 1200 degrees at full heat. She sold 39 bowls at the fair itself, and 2 more were chipped while being carried to the van. Half of her income comes from teaching classes. Each bowl she still had was wrapped in 5 sheets of tissue paper. All that tissue was then shared equally among 3 shipping crates, and she travelled with the crate bound for Leeds. Inside that crate the tissue was divided equally among 4 boxes, and she opened only the top box, whose sheets were spread equally over the 5 mugs it held. How many sheets were wrapped around the mug at the front of that box?

The lakeside campsite had 73 tents pitched at the end of August, and it quotes its fees in cents rather than in dollars. Departing families took down 46 of the tents over the bank holiday. A storm wrecked 3 more, which the warden folded away for scrap. The site is 15 kilometres from the nearest town. Every tent still standing sleeps 8 people, and the warden added the 55 sleeping places available in the wooden cabins. Each sleeping place was then booked solid for 3 nights of the festival. How many bed-nights were booked?

A toy factory had 116 boxes of building bricks in its despatch room and brought in 66 more from the moulding line. The factory weighs its bricks in grams rather than in kilograms. Every box in the despatch room contains 8 bricks. A worker found 49 loose bricks under the conveyor and added them to the count, and 39 bricks came back in a customer return. Inspectors then pulled out 58 bricks with faulty studs and scrapped them. How many bricks were in the despatch room?
